issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object. The template does not provide a StudentCount class or signature, and the problem text explicitly hints to check the UML return type. This mismatch introduces a structural inconsistency: students following the UML will implement/expect an int, whereas the solution wraps the count in a StudentCount type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (and remove StudentCount), or (b) update the problem statement UML and template to specify and provide the StudentCount type (including adding StudentCount.java to the template and documenting its use). Ensure the chosen approach is reflected in the template, the problem text/UML, and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (the total number of students represented as a primitive int), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning a StudentCount object and introduces a new StudentCount class. This represents the same conceptual entity (total number of students) with two different identifiers/representations across artifacts, which can confuse students who expect a simple int as described in the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation consistent: either change the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (sum of inscribed and guest students) to match the UML and problem description, removing the StudentCount wrapper; or update the problem statement/UML to document and explain the StudentCount type (and its usage) so students expect an object return type instead of a primitive.
